title: Differential Snapshot Backfiller with Safe Apply and Rate-Aware Throttling
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a differential snapshot backfiller to replay historical usage events into the console analytics pipeline while minimizing resource contention and ensuring idempotent application. This ticket covers: 1) creating exportable time-bucketed snapshots of processed state, 2) computing and applying diffs rather than full replays to downstream sinks (metrics, billing, routing), 3) an apply-safety layer that detects and safely skips already-applied patches, and 4) adaptive rate-aware throttling to avoid overloading ingestion buffers during high concurrency windows. The goal is to allow targeted backfills (by date ranges, customers, or event types) that are safe to run repeatedly and that can be paused/resumed with checkpoints.
acceptance_criteria: Backfiller can generate time-bucketed differential patches for a given date range and model of event granularity (minute/hour/day)
Applying a patch is idempotent: re-applying the same patch produces no duplicate metrics, billing adjustments, or downstream side effects
Tool exposes resume tokens and fine-grained progress metrics (events processed, patches applied, errors) to the console
Throttling controller automatically slows apply rate when ingest queue latency or downstream error rate exceeds thresholds
End-to-end integration tests and a canary run on a low-traffic customer dataset demonstrate correctness and safe rollback
steps: Design snapshot format and diff encoding (compact JSONL with checksums and version header)
Implement exporter that reads existing processed-state store and emits bucketed snapshots with metadata
Build diff generator that takes two snapshots and produces minimal change set with ops (insert/update/delete) and idempotency keys
Develop apply worker that validates patch checksums, applies ops within a transactional boundary when supported, and records resume tokens
Add rate-aware throttling: integrate with telemetry to observe ingest-latency and adjust worker concurrency and token bucket rates
Wire up observability: per-patch tracing, per-customer backfill dashboards, and alerting for skewed apply ratios
Create a runbook and safety checks for on-call to abort/inspect long-running backfills
